runs.content: Tuesday's rotation focus is AI & Tech + Technology, but neither domain has gained a new page since 2026-08-27, and log.md since the last thinker run (2026-08-31) shows almost no activity: a routine portfolio-management-briefing (no trades executed), a spinoff-monitor run (0 new candidates, just status updates on already-tracked names), and a single new ingest — books/book-breath.md, created today by the book-summarizer catch-up from Fred's reading list (read 2026-08-03). That last item produced the day's one genuinely new, non-duplicate find: [[health/source-godin-breathwork-2026]] (ingested 2026-05-15) explicitly names its own source in its metadata — 'Referenced book: Breath: The New Science of a Lost Art — James Nestor' — and its Mechanism section leans entirely on 'Nestor's research' as the evidentiary basis for the whole page. The newly-created [[books/book-breath]] independently restates the identical material (nasal vs. mouth breathing, ancient techniques anticipating modern science, breath as a stress-reduction lever) but its See Also section links only to reading-list.md and suggestions.md — nothing points back to the Health page it directly underlies, and the reverse link doesn't exist either. Logged as a new cross-domain connection (concrete next step: cross-link book-breath.md to health/source-godin-breathwork-2026.md and health/my-protocol.md, and add a reverse link from the source page's Cross-References). No new investigation idea cleared the bar today — AI & Tech/Technology's overview pages and recent source pages were checked against the rest of the wiki-map but turned up nothing not already logged in the existing Open Investigation Ideas list — and nothing in the existing open sections showed signs of resolution.

Monday's rotation focus is Finance + Crypto. Since the last thinker run (2026-08-30), log.md shows only routine activity: two Monday-morning trackers (sector-performance-tracker, growth-value-tracker) plus the prior day's memory-update and mf-update — no new clippings, podcast pages, book pages, or research artifacts landed anywhere in the wiki. Crypto's own portfolio page is unchanged since 2026-08-29 (no refresh due until Saturday). Deep-reading today's two tracker updates against the rest of Finance surfaced one genuinely new, non-duplicate gap: [[finance/market-sector-performance]]'s Cybersecurity (CIBR) entry reaccelerated sharply this run — Q3 partial nearly doubling from +4.2% to +9.7% in two trading days, lifting YTD to +38.3% and making it the tracker's best two-day mover, while sitting at 38.16x P/E in the tracker's 'Expensive' band. The page treats this purely as a momentum/valuation-band story with no fundamental context. But [[finance/investor-letters/source-burry-sw50-part2-productivity-cybersecurity-2026-05-28]] already ran Burry's own IV15/Composite Score valuation framework against CIBR's three largest constituents back in May: CrowdStrike ranks dead last (50/50) among 50 software names at 23.18x P/IV15 'despite a Castle tier,' explicitly flagged by the page itself as 'a useful counterpoint to any cybersecurity is AI-proof thesis' — Palo Alto and Zscaler also score poorly on valuation despite strong moats. Three months later the sector-level price action is doing exactly what that fundamental critique warned about, and neither page cites the other. Logged as a new investigation idea (concrete next step: add a line to market-sector-performance.md's CIBR entries citing the Burry SW50 valuation critique as the fundamental counterpoint behind the 'Expensive' flag, cross-linked both ways). No new cross-domain connection cleared the bar today (both today's changes stayed within Finance), and nothing in the existing Open Investigation Ideas / Cross-Domain Connections lists showed signs of resolution.
